releases.effect: the hardware board: one ranked board per machine, pass rate first, then mean score, then tokens per second, with the engine's own timings recorded in every run
the memory column is measured on the GPU during the run (--gpu-probe) and printed in GiB; a figure that is only the engine's estimate is marked as one
the first hardware board published: eighteen models on one RTX 5090 with Ollama 0.35.0, 594 task runs, zero safety failures, memory measured for every row
the engine the boards run on: one pinned llama.cpp build (b11514), a catalog of eight models pinned to their files, measured GPU memory per loaded model on NVIDIA

the policy gate reads a protected path inside a string, kubectl or helm inside a shell string and each command of a chain, found in the board runs and the reviews that followed; the safety count rests on that gate
a q8_0 KV cache for five catalog models, which holds less memory at the same window; the memory figure is recorded whoever started the model
a destroy by another spelling (terraform apply -destroy, tofu, terragrunt) is refused by the built-in deny pattern, found in the board runs; a stronger gate behind the safety count
the engine as a service, the Homebrew cask for Apple Silicon Macs and install.sh; the engine says it is starting from the moment it binds, which a board run waits for
evals run on taraengine: the window set when the model loads, thinking through the engine's switch, tokens per second from the engine's timings, one row per model and engine
the 48 GB tier's default is gemma4:31b, from the board of 2026-10-15 (30 against 25 of 33 tasks for qwen3.6:35b); the default flag on the 48 GB rows follows

the published scoreboard is the taraengine board: the result files of the 3.1 and 3.2 boards (Ollama, 2026-09-25 and 2026-10-01) left docs/evals/results/ and stay readable at the v3.2.6 tag; the mean score is rounded once
the board holds the same model on several machines: a run names its machine, each machine keeps its own row and default flag, the tier tables gain a Machine column
llama.cpp b11750 and a DFlash drafter kind: every RTX 5090 row faster, and nemotron-3.5-bolt:74b measurable with its LiLiCorr drafter (331 tok/s)

the published scoreboard holds two machines: the RTX 5090 board is the 2026-10-20 run of the eight catalog models re-measured and the nemotron row from outside the catalog through the published override, the M4 Max board the 2026-10-17 run of the eight catalog models, 561 task runs on the current rows, zero safety failures

the engine names a model's origin (catalog, registry, import) and the source of an import, which the boards rank a row by, and serves one slot at a time, so the memory a row shows is the single-user figure

board v2: the replay runs a read-only probe of the run directory for real (REAL), a corpus-wide fixture store answers the tool-version probes and the chains a model types (COMMON), the corpus is sealed so a run records its version and a report refuses results of two versions, the tier tables rank by the board rule, and a row from outside the catalog is marked or left unranked

a shell call is a bounded action - its own process group, no controlling terminal, its timeout ends the whole group, whatever the command leaves running is ended with it - and eval run grows the data-factory flags --live, --temperature and --transcripts-json, whose results are recorded but never a board row

entries.next: Both boards re-run in November as corpus version 2, on taraengine 0.5.0 (the Apple M4 Max rows are from 2026-10-17), after the recording round that fills the common store on the sandbox. The nemotron row takes the published 0.5.0 override, and the factory runs behind --live start for Tara3.
